I checked the proposal and made one fix: the title carried the agent role ("you are a mastermind, on Sonnet, high effort"). I moved that to an italic line under the title.

- **Text check:** `text-check.mjs` flagged nothing.
- **Asks:** the five asks are listed unticked, which is right for a proposal.
- **Unfixed:** module names such as `core/Plugin`, Recite and Dictate are still plain text, not links. I left them, since this is an agent-facing brief and the proposal has no owner running to send the rewrite to.
- **Not checked:** the proposal has no `page.js`, so I took no screenshots.

I logged the result as `rewrote` in `flags.jsonl`.

I wrote the review to `public/framework/ai/sessions/2026/10/20/session-e00f55c9/chat-settings-per-session/review.md`, and the verdict is **fix**. I did not run the tests or the code, and I made no edits.

- **Scope:** the diff covers only step 1, instance-level plugins in `core/Plugin`. The Voice Chat plugins, the Chat settings panel, saving with the session and the Make default button are not in it. All five asks in `requirements.md` are still unticked.
- **Handover:** the task folder doesn't say what landed and what is still open, so a fresh agent couldn't continue from it. I asked for a status section in `plan.md`.
- **Two code gaps in `Plugin.js`:**
  - Instances that override a plugin on at the class level aren't tracked after a class-level disable and enable.
  - `make_default` skips re-attaching other instances for plugins that have a config but no `fields`.
- **Smaller notes:**
  - One test in `Plugin.test.mjs` asserts nothing.
  - `plan.md` calls the attached set `inst.attached`, but the code keeps it under a symbol.
  - The readme's Structure bullet for `Plugin.js` doesn't mention the new instance methods.
  - The per-instance state is created lazily in three places.

I wrote the review to `chat-settings-per-session/review.md` with verdict `fix`. I made no code edits.

This diff covers only step 1 of five: the instance level of `core/Plugin`. That part is sound, and all 24 tests pass in worktree qf-4. Four of the owner's five asks are not built: the Voice Chat plugins, the Chat settings panel, saving with the session, and the Make default button. Ask 2 is met only inside `core/Plugin`, since no Voice Chat plugin uses it yet.

The `[fix]` findings:
1. **Task scope:** the task folder must stay open, because steps 2 to 5 are still to do and no box in `requirements.md` can be ticked.
2. **`files.jsonl`:** `core/Plugin/files.jsonl` now lists `failures.jsonl` twice and also marks it "gone", though the file still exists.
3. **Stale doc:** `core/Plugin/doc/design-notes.md:16` says instances are tracked only for plugins with their own `detach`, which no longer matches the code.
4. **`make_default`:** when it turns a plugin on at the class, other instances that are already open never get it (`Plugin.js:105-127`).

I added four `[note]` findings, covering unneeded re-attach churn, one dead check, a simplicity remark and the doc counts that check out.

I accepted both declines and wrote them to `review/reply.md` in the chat-settings-per-session task folder.

- **Finding 1:** accept. This is merge 1 of 5, `plan.md` Status says so honestly, and the folder stays open with no ask ticked.
- **Finding 6:** accept, but on the author's stated reason only. I did not re-read `Plugin.js`, so I did not check the code myself. The reason is that an earlier plugin attach or the constructor args can load overrides before the "new" hook runs, and the comment now says so.

My verdict is **fix**: this merge's code is sound, but the task folder misdescribes it in two places. I wrote the report to `chat-settings-per-session/review.md`. I only read the diff and didn't run its test file.

This diff is the Servex half of steps 4 and 5. It stores each session's plugin settings and adds one shared "Make default" store, `/api/session/defaults`. It changes no page.

**Fixes:**
1. **Plan is out of date:** the Status section of `plan.md` doesn't mention this merge (worktree `chat-settings-servex`, commit 9a39ff44a), so a fresh agent can't tell from the folder what's built or what comes next.
2. **Doc describes unbuilt code:** `ux/Dictate/doc/settings.md` says a page reads the defaults at load, with `localStorage` as the fallback. No page code calls `/api/session/defaults` yet.

**Notes:**
- **Partial write on a refused setting:** in `Sessions.settings()`, `plugins` is written before the assistant and wake settings are checked. If one of those is refused, the new `plugins` stays in memory and gets saved on the next save. The code comment claims a refused value leaves nothing behind, which is only true when `plugins` itself is refused.
- **Not indexed:** `Servex/agents/readme.md` doesn't list the new test file or the new route.
- **Asks:** none of the owner's five asks is met yet. Two are partly done: settings now persist per session on Servex, and the "Make default" store exists, but there is no button. Leaving them unticked is right.
- **Simpler way:** I don't see a simpler design. Reusing the existing per-session settings route plus one small defaults file is what the brief asked for.

The review passes. This merge is the server half of steps 4 and 5 (Servex is the background server): each voice session can save its own plugin settings, and there is one shared set of defaults. In worktree `chat-settings-servex` (commit 7d32afd51), `node Servex/agents/Sessions.plugins.test.mjs` passes all 4 checks.

- **The owner's asks:** none of the five is met yet. The settings store and the defaults store for asks 4 and 5 work on the server, but nothing on the page uses them and there is no "Make default" button. `plan.md` says this plainly and the task stays open, so it counts as an honest partial merge, not a miss.
- **The earlier review's fixes are in place:**
  - The `plugins` value is checked first and saved only after the other settings pass their checks.
  - The new test and the defaults route are listed in `Servex/agents/readme.md`.
  - `ux/Dictate/doc/settings.md` says the page side isn't built.
  - The new `GET /api/session/defaults` is registered before `/api/session/:id` (`Sessions.js:1757`), so "defaults" isn't mistaken for a session id.
- **Three notes, no fixes:**
  - One line in `plan.md` Status still says the page "reads" the defaults at load, as if that were built. It should say "will read".
  - Changing the assistant mode is still saved before the other settings are checked. That order was there before this diff.
  - There is no simpler way to do this.
- **Can a fresh agent continue?** Yes. `plan.md` Status names the worktree, the commits and the steps still open.

The report is at `public/framework/ai/sessions/2026/10/20/session-e00f55c9/chat-settings-per-session/review.md`.

The verdict is **fix**: the code itself is sound, but the plan is stale and the Plugin page doesn't show the new per-instance state. The report is at `…/chat-settings-per-session/review/report.md`. I made no code edits.

**Fixes:**
1. **`plan.md` is stale.** Its Status still lists the step 1 remainder as open, but commit a9a75d7df built it. Steps 2, 4 and 5 still tell the next builder to call `plugin_state` and `set_plugin`, and neither exists; what was built is `inst.plugins.find().get/set`, `inst.overrides`, `load_overrides`, `reset_plugins` and `Host.make_default`. A fresh agent following the plan would code against methods that aren't there.
2. **The Plugin page doesn't show the new state.** `Plugin` can now hold settings per instance, but `/framework/core/Plugin/` shows only the class-level list. It has no live instances, no per-instance overrides, and no Make default or Reset to default.

**Notes:**
- `ux/Dictate/doc/settings-plugins.md` still describes only the per-instance on/off switch, not the new per-instance config, `overrides` or `make_default`.
- **Tests:**
  - The core/Plugin tests pass, 28 of 28, matching the readme.
  - The Servex test couldn't run in this worktree because `Servex/node_modules` is missing (`npm ci` is needed). It already passed 4 of 4 on the earlier merge.
- **Owner's asks:**
  - Asks 2, 4 and 5 are partly met: the core and the Servex store exist, but nothing on the page uses them yet.
  - Asks 1 and 3 (Voice Chat plugins, the Chat settings panel) aren't built.
- **The screenshots don't show this work:**
  - The saved diff was cut from an older starting point, so it pulled in about 100 session-log files, and the reviewer screenshotted those pages instead.
  - Seven of the ten are 404s. They come from a stray `public/public/` folder that the Servex log sweeps write to the wrong path. It's already on michael/dev, not something this branch added, but that write path still needs fixing.

The report is written to `review/report.md` in the task folder, with `verdict: fix`. I made no code edits.

- **Requirements:** The diff builds only step 1, the instance-level plugins in `core/Plugin`. Asks 1 and 3 are not met, and 2, 4 and 5 are only partly met. The Voice Chat plugins, the Chat settings panel, the Make default button in Chat and the page-side save and load are all unbuilt.
- **`plan.md` is stale:** Its Status says step 1 merges after qf-1 lands, but qf-1 has already landed (merge d5af6b3c0).
- **Shots are noisy:** Only the `core/Plugin` shots show this diff. The other nine shot folders are seven 404 pages and two or three unrelated session pages.
- **Wrapping:** The `Make default` and `Reset to default` buttons on the Plugin demo wrap to two lines at 1200, 1920 and 3440.
- **Notes:** The framework readme's one-line `core/Plugin` entry doesn't mention per-instance overrides or Make default. The Plugin page is 70 to 79% empty at the wide widths, which is normal for a prose page.

I didn't read the questions.md files first, so the system sections answer from my own judgement of the shots and `layout.json`.

I finished the review and the verdict is **fix**. This merge does part of step 2: Interrupt and Thinking cue are now plugins on core/Plugin, and `chat.js` connects them. Both the VoiceChat tests (10 of 10) and the core/Plugin tests pass, and the new files are indexed.

**Fixes:**
1. **Settings aren't really per chat.** Every chat box creates its own VoiceChat, but they all write to the same shared read-aloud object (`Recite.shared.barge`). On a page with two chats, whichever was set up last wins. The test only passes because each chat there gets its own fake object.
2. **Button handlers pile up.** `Interrupt.bind()` wraps the bar's on/off, mode and threshold handlers again each time a chat is set up (`Interrupt.js:182`). So one click updates every chat's settings, and a chat that is set up again (a re-render or a session switch) adds another wrapper that is never cleaned up.
3. **The threshold slider keeps reopening the mic.** Each move of the slider turns the plugin off and back on, which closes and reopens the mic while a reply is being read aloud (`ReciteBar.js:44` → `BargeIn.js:91`).
4. **`plan.md` is out of date.** Its Status still says step 2 hasn't been started and doesn't list the four plugins still to build. A fresh agent reading the folder would port the earlier build (Merge A) a second time.

**Notes:**
- When a chat opens, Interrupt switches on briefly before the browser's saved "off" is applied, which can open the mic for a moment if a reply is playing.
- None of the five asks can be ticked yet, and the brief correctly ticks none.

The review is in `chat-settings-per-session/review.md`.

The verdict is **fix**: the code works, but three docs are stale or contradict it. I ran both test suites and all pass: 12/12 VoiceChat and 30/30 core/Plugin. The report is in `chat-settings-per-session/review.md`.

**Fixes needed:**
1. **A doc tells agents to delete the new code.** `ux/Dictate/doc/settings-plugins.md:16` still says "Delete/ignore `ux/Dictate/VoiceChat/VoiceChat.js`". That path is now the new VoiceChat class this diff adds.
2. **"One per chat" versus "one per page."** `ux/Dictate/readme.md:101` and the header comments in `VoiceChat.js` and `VoiceChat.test.mjs` say there is one VoiceChat per chat. `chat.js` and the VoiceChat readme say what the code does: one per Recite, shared by every chat on the page.
3. **Settings changes are described the old way.** `settings-plugins.md` and step 1 of `plan.md` still say a settings change detaches and re-attaches the plugin. core/Plugin now calls a plugin's own `reconfigure` method when it has one. The next plugin port needs that for anything that keeps a mic or timer open.

**Notes (no change needed now):**
- **Partial delivery is expected.** This is merge 3, the first group of step 2. Only the "plugins" and "set per instance" asks are partly met, and only for Interrupt and ThinkingCue. The Chat settings panel, saving with the session and the Make default button are not built yet. `plan.md` says so and ticks none of the owner's five asks.
- **Interrupt's defaults are written twice.** They repeat the values Recite's barge-in code already holds.
- **One untested edge case.** Turning Interrupt back on doesn't reset barge-in's "heard" state the way the bar's own on switch does.
- **The bar's switch saves a setting even when it matches the default.** That chat then stops following a later Make default for that switch.
- **Make default wouldn't survive a reload.** The chat page still keeps plugin defaults in memory rather than the browser's storage; that comes with the page side of step 5.
- **Unrelated lines in three `files.jsonl` files.** Each has a "`failures.jsonl` gone" entry that this task didn't cause.

No screenshots came with this diff, so I answered only Requirements and Words. I made no code edits.

Logged. Done.

**core/Settings built and committed** — commit `915342569` in `worktree/chat-settings-settings`.

- `Settings.js`, `Settings.test.mjs` (12 tests, 31 checks, all green), `readme.md`, `page.js` (live demo), one index line in `public/framework/readme.md`.
- Demo shots at 360×740 and 1920×2000 both read clean: toggle, slider with end text, number, select with help text, two groups, live `own` JSON. `check_page`: no JS errors.
- Nothing from the brief skipped. One judgment call: `make_default()` also updates `this.defaults` in place (not just returns the merge), so `get()` stays consistent on the same instance afterward — the brief's "the caller stores the returned defaults" reads as about the level above, not a contradiction.

Full detail is logged at `public/framework/ai/sessions/2026/11/03/session-9d296611/minion-settings-build-step3/session.jsonl`.

My verdict on step 3 (the new `core/Settings` module) is **fix**: the full report is in `review/report.md` in the task folder. I made no code edits.

**Three things to fix:**
1. **Opening a session saves it again.** `load()` is meant never to save, but each group (`dictate`, `recite`) passes its change up to the parent, and the parent schedules a save (`Settings.js` line 34). So opening a session with grouped settings writes them back to `session.jsonl` 400 ms later. The tests only check `load()` without groups, so they don't catch this.
2. **The slider is too small at 1920.** On the demo page the Volume slider is about 60 px wide. The label takes the spare room and the slider never grows. The Chat settings panel will be drawn by this same `render()`, and its thresholds are sliders, so this would show up there too.
3. **A fresh agent couldn't pick this up from the task folder.** The Status section of `plan.md` has no line for step 3: no worktree, no commit, nothing saying it's in review.

**Smaller notes:**
- The code sample is cut off at the right edge at 400 and 1920.
- The demo says the JSON is "on the right", but at 400 it sits below the panel.
- The line saying which settings you're editing reads "this session" in small grey text, which is easy to miss.
- The rows are spaced loosely, about 68 px apart, for a panel meant for a phone.

**What's met for this step:** the four field types (toggle, slider, number, dropdown), the `dictate` and `recite` groups, text at both ends of every slider, help text under a dropdown, `make_default()`, and the module is listed in the framework readme. None of the owner's five asks is ticked yet, and that's correct: the panel, saving with the session and the buttons come in steps 4 and 5.

I was given all four widths (400, 1200, 1920 and 3440), each with its layout numbers.

The review verdict is **fix**, for two small doc gaps. The code meets the brief's step 3 (`core/Settings`). The report is at `chat-settings-per-session/review/report.md`.

**Fixes:**
1. **Settings is missing from the core index.** `core/readme.md`, which lists every core module, has no line for it. The framework readme and `core/files.jsonl` do list it.
2. **The test count in the readme is out of date.** `core/Settings/readme.md` says 12 tests, but the test file now has 13, and `plan.md` also says 13. The new test for loading grouped settings was never added to the count.

**Notes:**
- **The screenshots are older than the fixes.** They were taken at 14:23, before the two fix commits from the last review round. They still show the old problems: the 60 px slider, the faint "this session" line, the words "on the right", and the cut-off code sample. So I checked those fixes against the diff, not the pictures. A new set of screenshots would confirm them.
- **The code sample may still be cut off on a phone.** Its lines are about 60 characters long, so at 400 px wide it will probably still clip.
- **The dropdown's help text lands under the bottom bar at 400 px.** It sits in a column under the dropdown; on its own full-width line, like the other fields' help, it would read better.

**On your other questions:** none of the five owner asks is ticked yet, which is right for merge 4 of 7. The demo page shows a live instance with its saved settings updating beside it. And a fresh agent could carry on from the task folder alone: `plan.md` now records the worktree, the commit and the next step.
